content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns
content.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 18 & \sqrt{6} & \sqrt{3} & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -10 & 4\end{aligned}|
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The $A$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain

$$
|A|=2\cdot 1\cdot 1\cdot 4=8\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has identical columns:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- Since $C$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix, its determinant is:

$$
det(C)=5\cdot 4-(-2)\cdot (-10)=0
$$

Therefore, only $|B|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{5} & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}4 & \sqrt{3} & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}|
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has a zero column: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{5} & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- Since $B$ is a diagonal matrix, we obtain 

$$
|B|=3\cdot (-1)\cdot 5=-15\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has identical columns: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & \sqrt{3} & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|C|=0.$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

after.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 0 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{3} & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 6 & \sqrt{3} & 3 \\ -4 & \sqrt{7} & -2\end{aligned}|.

after.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has a zero row: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- The matrix $B$ is a triangular matrix, hence 

$$
|B|=2\cdot (-5)\cdot 4=-40\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has proportional columns: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 6 & \sqrt{3} & 3 \\ -4 & \sqrt{7} & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|C|=0.$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$
